**The meaning of the verse**
﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهَا وَإِذَا حَكَمْتُم بَيْنَ النَّاسِ أَن تَحْكُمُوا بِالْعَدْلِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُم بِهِ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا﴾
Allah the Exalted commands you to give back the various trusts you have been entrusted with to their owners, and not to neglect them; and He commands you to judge between people with justice and fairness when you judge between them. How excellent is what Allah admonishes you with and guides you to! Allah the Exalted is All-Hearing of your words, aware of all your deeds, All-Seeing of them.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. Ayham said, "Who'll ever know?" and Tariq said, "I'll know." What did Tariq mean?
2. The family was in hardship and the gold was in the chest. Why would taking from it not have been a "loan" to be paid back in the spring? (Because the money belonged to someone else and its owner had not given permission, and using a trust without the owner's permission is betrayal, even if the one keeping it intends to give it back.)
3. What did Tariq's mother do instead of taking from the pouch? And what did the whole household gain when Abu Mundhir came back?

**This week's exercise**
Give your child a real trust: one of your things, or a small sum of money in a sealed envelope, which they keep for a week and then give back to you just as they received it. And this week let them give back everything they have borrowed from their brothers, sisters or friends.
